findings.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ClientRemovedEvent listener still calls it when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (AdminPermissions.java ~88-90), breaking all client deletions with a 500 and preventing cleanup of per-client permission resources

canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 (~147-155) throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a policy decision or false, causing a hard 500 on the token endpoint for every token exchange attempt when the feature flag is enabled, with no V2-safe way to guard the call since isPermissionsEnabled also throws

canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 (~90-103) drop the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role shortcut that V1 included, so admins holding the standard manage-clients role are denied (403) on role-mapping operations they could previously perform

Feature-gating the removal-cleanup listener in AdminPermissions.java (~77) with Profile.isFeatureEnabled skips cleanup of leftover authorization resources/policies for deleted roles/clients/groups when the feature is disabled, leaving orphaned authz data with no reclamation path

Client-removal cleanup is wired to a throwing stub: the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in V2 mode (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled — the PR's target mode and Keycloak's default) lands on ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, so either DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with 500/rollback for every client in FGAP-enabled realms, or if the exception is swallowed the deleted client's authz Resource (named by internal ID), scopes, and attached scope-permissions/policies are permanently orphaned with no working per-client cleanup path anywhere in V2.

Runtime token-exchange permission check throws instead of evaluating: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, so a grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange request reaching the exchange-permission check in FGAP-enabled realms produces an unhandled 500 instead of an allow/deny decision (security control failing open with a server error rather than denying), previously-configured V1 exchange grants become inoperative, and the new CLIENTS resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema omits the V1 token-exchange scope entirely so the exchange permission can no longer even be created.

Other throwing overrides in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, *Permission) will 500 any remaining caller of the legacy per-client permissions API (e.g., the old admin console 'Permissions' tab) in V2 realms.

Map-roles checks lost the V1 'manage ⇒ map-roles' equivalence with no admin-role fallback: V2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles accept only an explicit map-roles/map-roles-composite/map-roles-client-scope FGAP grant, so neither the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role nor a per-client manage/configure grant satisfies them, potentially silently denying routine client-role operations (e.g., composite-role management) to standard realm admins and even full realm admins without explicit FGAP grants in every FGAP-enabled (default) realm — intent and out-of-diff call sites must be verified before merge.

getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:125-145) performs an unbounded findByType scan of every Clients-type resource in the realm's admin resource server, running a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per resource — including potential lazy loads from resource.getScopes() inside the loop — and materializing the entire granted set into a HashSet regardless of the request's pagination; this N+1 pattern costs O(#client-resources × evaluation cost) on every admin client list request, recomputed from scratch each time even though permission grants rarely change

Permission checks in ClientPermissionsV2 (lines 57-88, 117-122, ~213-221) run redundant, un-memoized full evaluations within a single check: a denied canView(client) triggers up to four independent full evaluations, canView(ClientScopeModel) evaluates the same type resource twice when one evaluation's returned Collection<Permission> already contains every granted scope, and hasPermission(ClientModel, String) issues a policy-store findByResource emptiness probe whose answer the subsequent evaluation would already provide; nothing caches type-resource or per-client evaluation results, multiplying the cost on the hot admin path where getAccess flows call several canXxx methods per client

ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is incompatible with V2's throwing setPermissionsEnabled: the AdminPermissions.java listener (~78-95) still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on client removal, which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 (~191-195); if the listener receives the V2 evaluator while FGAP is enabled, every client deletion throws from inside the event listener and rolls back the delete, and if it receives the V1 implementation, V2 type-'Clients' resources and their associated policies for deleted clients are never (or only partially) cleaned up, accumulating orphaned authz rows without bound

Removal-event cleanup in AdminPermissions.java:78 is now gated on the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag (previously it ran unconditionally), so a deployment that used FGAP and later disables the feature will leak resource/policy rows for every subsequently removed client, role, or group — inert rows that grow the authz tables without bound and slow findByType scans if the feature is ever re-enabled

P1: Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException whenever V2 is active — the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.java (~89-95) still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but with the feature enabled clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws 'Not supported in V2', causing DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} to fail with 500 and a rolled-back transaction (and leaking per-client 'Clients' permission resources if the exception is swallowed); the V2 override should clean up or no-op, never throw from a listener-invoked method.

P2: UnsupportedOperationException thrown from runtime permission evaluators instead of failing closed — canExchangeTo (ClientPermissionsV2.java:147) and the rest of the UOE family (~151-204: exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) are runtime evaluator surfaces consulted by V1 cross-client token-exchange and admin REST endpoints (getAccess, per-client management-permission endpoints); throwing converts what should be a deny (403) or feature-gated 4xx into an HTTP 500 whenever V2 is active — permission checks must fail closed (return false) or the call sites must be provably unreachable/gated in V2 mode.

P2: Feature-gating the removal listener (AdminPermissions.java ~78) silently disables permission-resource cleanup in the default feature-off mode — previously RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handlers ran unconditionally deleting removed entities' V1 permission resources and dependent policies from the realm-management authorization server; now with the flag off (the default for a preview feature) nothing is cleaned, and with the flag on the roles()/groups() branches run V1 implementations against the V2 resource server (root.realmResourceServer()), so V1 cleanup effectively never happens in either mode, accumulating orphaned resources/policies unboundedly; if V1 permission management is dead the listener body should be removed rather than gated.

P3: Enabling the feature flips client-permission semantics with no migration for existing V1 grants — V2 evaluators (ClientPermissionsV2.java:63-121: canManage/canView/canConfigure/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles, via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()) consult only admin roles plus the new 'Clients' schema store and do not consult V1 per-client grants (realm-management manage/configure/view/map-roles scopes), so flipping the preview feature on silently revokes those grants (allow → deny, operations start returning 403) with no migration step, error hint, or release-note documentation visible; needs an explicit migration/doc note or a compatibility evaluation during the V1→V2 transition.

Client deletion with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled routes the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener (AdminPermissions.java ~90-92) into ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (~191-194), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException — since the listener guard and the V2 selection share the same feature flag, every client deletion either propagates the exception and fails/rolls back DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}, or the exception is swallowed and cleanup silently never runs while logging a stack trace

No resource lifecycle for per-client permission resources: AdminPermissionsSchema getOrCreateResource/resolveClient create per-client resources but nothing ever deletes a client's resource (or its scope-permission policies) when the client is removed, causing unbounded growth of orphaned authorization store rows, wasted hasGrantedPermission evaluation of stale resources on every filtered client listing in getClientsWithPermission (which can surface deleted clients' UUIDs in the granted set), and findByName lookups hitting dead rows

V2 UnsupportedOperationException stubs in ClientPermissionsV2 (~150-204: canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRoles*Permission, resource, getPermissions) remain reachable from live request paths outside the new model — token exchange and the legacy client management-permissions REST endpoints now hit unhandled UOE resulting in HTTP 500 instead of the previously inherited functioning V1 implementations, with the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import and dead getEvaluationContext (~260) indicating unfinished stub work
The Clients ResourceType omits a token-exchange scope entirely, so with both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and TOKEN_EXCHANGE enabled, token exchanges can neither be granted nor denied gracefully

The feature gate in AdminPermissions.java (~78) silently disables stale-resource cleanup when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is off: the role/client/group cleanup listener previously ran unconditionally but is now skipped, so deployments that previously enabled FGAP and later disabled the feature no longer clean up leftover authorization data on role/client/group deletions

hasPermission(ClientModel, String)'s fallback calls getResourceTypeResource, which can create the type resource as a side effect of a read-only permission check (writes-on-read), though it mirrors the existing users V2 pattern and is idempotent

ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles check only the explicit fine-grained scope with no MANAGE_CLIENTS role check or canManage(client) fallback (unlike V1 which delegated map-roles to manage), silently dropping the 'manage implies map-roles' contract — nothing pins this behavior, and a plain manage-clients admin could get 403 on role mapping under V2; either the implication is intended (needs a test asserting manage ⇒ map-roles) or it's a bug (needs a fix)

MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope is added but never tested anywhere — the test class doesn't import it, no test grants or denies it, and the client scope-mappings role path it guards (canMapClientScopeRoles) is never exercised, so broken wiring for this scope would go undetected

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and CONFIGURE in a single permission and then asserts addComposites succeeds, so it cannot detect wrong-scope enforcement (it would still pass if the endpoint enforced MAP_ROLES or CONFIGURE instead of MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE); a negative test granting MAP_ROLES+CONFIGURE only and asserting addComposites → 403 is required

The CONFIGURE vs MANAGE boundary for client update is untested — testConfigureOnlyOneClient never attempts clientResource.update(...) after granting only CONFIGURE, and update is only covered under MANAGE, so if the update endpoint or canConfigure accidentally allowed full client updates for configure-only users no test would fail

Thirteen V1 API surface methods (canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, managePermission, viewPermission, resource, getPermissions, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException when V2 is active, but no test asserts callers/endpoints handle this gracefully rather than 500-ing, nor that token exchange behaves sanely under V2 config — this entire reachable surface ships unverified

The reworked registerListener removal-cleanup path in AdminPermissions.java is untested — no test exercises deletion of a client that has V2 permission resources/policies attached and asserts they're cleaned up (or that deletion doesn't error), and since V2's setPermissionsEnabled throws, whether the listener dispatches to V1 or V2 on ClientRemovedEvent is safety-critical and unverified

Tests permanently mutate shared state without restoring it (myclient is renamed and has a default client scope removed/re-added as optional, myadmin gets client roles and composite mappings never removed, roles myclient-role/myclient-subRole are never cleaned), creating JUnit method-order dependence where a reorder or new intervening test can produce unrelated failures and the token-scope mutation can silently change authorization behavior in later tests

resolveClient's clientId-string fallback lookup path in AdminPermissionsSchema is untested — no client test creates a permission using the client's clientId string (all use myclient.getId()), so the fallback could be dead or broken (or collide when one client's clientId equals another entity's identifier) without detection

No negative/other-user policy enforcement tests for the Clients permission type — every client test grants a policy that matches the caller, and there is no test where the permission's policy targets a different user asserting the caller is still denied, so it's unproven that policies are actually enforced rather than resource existence granting access

Permission-evaluation logic copy-pasted three times in ClientPermissionsV2 (lines 221-231, 246-257, 273-283): the 'evaluate ResourcePermission -> nested loop -> match scope' block is duplicated verbatim in hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String), and the isAdminSameRealm()/realmResourceServer() guard preamble appears 4x (including getClientsWithPermission); the copies have already drifted (expectedScopes.contains(s) with a gratuitous single-element Arrays.asList(scope) vs. scope.equals(s)). This security-critical V2 FGAP core means any semantic fix must be applied in 3+ places, and the idiom is presumably mirrored again in UserPermissionsV2, multiplying drift. Extract one shared helper (e.g., on MgmtPermissionsV2).

ClientPermissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator mixes three concerns — permission evaluation, V1 per-entity permission-resource management, and V1 token-exchange wiring — so ClientPermissionsV2 must stub 12 inherited methods with UnsupportedOperationException (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions), an LSP violation; setPermissionsEnabled — a management mutator — even sits on the evaluator interface (ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:33). Split the interface (evaluation vs. management).

The ClientRemovedEvent branch in AdminPermissions (~line 92) still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 stubs to throw, while this PR re-wires MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() (lines 63-69) to return the V2 class and the removal listener is gated by the fine-grained-authz feature flag; if AdminPermissions.management() resolves to the V2 root in feature-enabled deployments, every client deletion throws mid-delete (a P1-level risk). Similar latent exposure exists for canExchangeTo (token-exchange flow) and the V1 permission-management endpoints. Make the listener resilient (no-op or real cleanup in V2) instead of throwing.

ClientPermissionsV2 has no resource-cleanup path: orphaned per-client 'Clients' resources accumulate, and even if the removal listener currently routes to V1, cleanup of V2-shaped data depends on the V1 class the V2 stubs disclaim — an undocumented cross-version dependency.

Dead code copied from V1 into ClientPermissionsV2: unused logger field (line 51), never-called private getEvaluationContext method (lines 260-270), unused static import TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46), unused org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope import (line 27), and ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports (lines 22-23, 29) referenced only by the dead method. A dead private helper that builds an evaluation context suggests behavior that doesn't exist and maintainers will trace or 'revive' it. Delete the cluster.

ClientPermissionEvaluator's public interface docs (lines 35-176) are made implementation-conditional: every new javadoc carries 'For V2 only: ...' clauses and {@link}s to AdminPermissionsSchema, ClientPermissionManagement (CONFIGURE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_*), and AdminPermissionManagement (MANAGE_SCOPE/VIEW_SCOPE) internals, so the public abstraction documents two divergent contracts wired to both implementations' constants; interface callers shouldn't need to know which version they hold, and when V1 is removed ~20 doc blocks must be rewritten and the links break (possibly already dangling). Keep interface docs implementation-agnostic and move version detail to the impls.

Persisted scope identifiers defined in two places: AdminPermissionsSchema (~lines 64-66) defines CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE while V1's ClientPermissionManagement defines CONFIGURE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE_SCOPE; these strings are persisted as scope names in the DB, so both definitions must stay byte-identical forever with nothing enforcing it. Have V1 reference the schema constants (services can depend on server-spi-private) instead of redefining them.

Two inconsistent code paths for the same 'all-clients' type resource in ClientPermissionsV2: the global path (line 241) uses resourceStore.findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) and denies if absent, while the per-client fallback (lines 214-218) uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) plus a policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() pre-check that exists only there; if getResourceTypeResource is get-or-create, a read-only permission check performs a write, and if it can return null, the subsequent findByResource(server, null) NPEs. The implicit invariant (type-level permissions are resource-linked so findByResource sees them) is undocumented and holds in only one path, so future edits to one path will silently diverge from the other.

PermissionClientTest tests mutate shared managed state without restoring it: testManageOnlyOneClient (~lines 155-175) permanently renames the shared managed client 'myclient' and removes one of its default client scopes (re-added only as optional), and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient (~lines 298-366) creates client roles with no cleanup while onAfter (lines 75-79) only deletes scope permissions; JUnit method order is non-deterministic within the class, so index-based picks (getDefaultClientScopes().get(0/1)) and any future count assertions become order-dependent. Restore mutated state or use per-test clients/scopes.

Inconsistent test-helper API after static-ization in AbstractPermissionTest (lines 54-76, ~116-178): helpers were converted to static and take ManagedClient/ManagedRealm parameters duplicating the base class's own injected client/realm fields (~30 call sites now spell createUserPolicy(realm, client, ...)), yet getPolicies() still uses the instance field, and the new createPermission(ManagedClient, String, String, Set, ...) overloads are instance methods touching no instance state while sibling createAllPermission is static; the mixed static/instance API plus redundant parameter passing invites passing a different ManagedClient than the injected one. Pick one style.

Deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException when admin-fine-grained-authz is enabled: the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws unconditionally, so every client deletion (admin console, REST, realm import) fails with a 500/rollback — a breakage introduced by this PR since V1 no-op'd gracefully. The PR's own PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients performs a client deletion, so either that test is red or unseen wiring suppresses the handler; both need to be verified.

V2 has no cleanup path at all for per-client Clients resources/policies on client deletion: getOrCreateResource lazily creates them, but all the resource-management methods throw, so orphaned resources/policies accumulate and keep being evaluated in getClientsWithPermission() forever.

Token exchange-to flows return a 500 instead of an allow/deny decision when the feature is enabled: canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 is a runtime enforcement point invoked by TokenExchangeManager on the exchange-to path, but the V2 override throws unconditionally.

The throwing method family in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRoles*Permission) must be confirmed unreachable from still-exposed REST endpoints such as the legacy /clients/{id}/managementPermissions — those call sites are in the truncated part of the diff.

Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2 indicating an unfinished port: an unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import and an orphaned private getEvaluationContext method that existed solely to build the client-identity evaluation context for exchange.

MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role shortcut silently dropped from canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles: V1 short-circuited on hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), but the V2 methods return only hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES*), so a plain manage-clients admin (and even realm-admin) gets 403 assigning client roles, adding role composites, or mapping client-scope roles — a silent privilege regression on feature-enable with no test coverage, and the new interface javadoc misdescribes V1 behavior.

Feature-gating the removal-event listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) stops legacy V1 resource cleanup when the feature is disabled (the default): realms using legacy per-object permissions will permanently orphan authz resources/policies/scopes in the admin resource server whenever a role/client/group with permissions enabled is deleted.

getClientsWithPermission() pollutes the granted-id set: resourceStore.findByType(server, 'Clients') also visits the type resource itself, so when an all-clients permission grants the scope the literal string 'Clients' is added to a set documented as containing client ids.

getClientsWithPermission() never enumerates clients authorized only via the all-clients type resource — it returns nothing useful exactly when the admin holds a realm-wide grant, so consumers relying on this set alone render silently empty lists (only the per-client MANAGE-scope path is covered by testManageOnlyOneClient).

Check-then-create race in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource: there is no uniqueness enforcement on resource names, so two concurrent permission creations referencing the same client (or concurrent lazy creation of the 'Clients' type resource on deny paths) can create duplicate same-named resources; subsequent findByName lookups return an arbitrary duplicate, making grants attached to one copy intermittently invisible to hasPermission (fail-closed, hard-to-reproduce 403s). This PR widens the race's blast radius to every per-client permission check and makes deny paths perform store writes as a side effect.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ClientRemovedEvent listener still calls it when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (AdminPermissions.java ~88-90), breaking all client deletions with a 500 and preventing cleanup of per-client permission resources

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). At the same time, the provider event listener in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` still invokes `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled (the call remains, just wrapped by the feature flag). `MgmtPermissionsV2` now overrides `clients()` to return a `ClientPermissionsV2` instance, so under the V2 permissions path this listener will call the unsupported method and can crash client removal handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 (~147-155) throw UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning a policy decision or false, causing a hard 500 on the token endpoint for every token exchange attempt when the feature flag is enabled, with no V2-safe way to guard the call since isPermissionsEnabled also throws

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that ClientPermissionsV2 explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException for canExchangeTo/exchangeToPermission (and several other methods like isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions). That creates a concrete risk of runtime failures if any V2 code path invokes these methods without an explicit V2-aware guard. However, the finding’s specific claim that this will cause a 500 on the token endpoint for “every token exchange attempt” when a feature flag is enabled is not verifiable from this diff because no call sites (e.g., token endpoint/token exchange flow) are shown here.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added ClientPermissionsV2, canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, scope) and do not include the admin-role short-circuit used elsewhere in V2 (e.g., canManage(ClientModel) and canManageClientScopes() both return true when root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)). This means a caller with the standard MANAGE_CLIENTS realm admin role but without the corresponding fine-grained permission will be denied by these canMap* checks, which is an inconsistent and likely breaking change in authorization behavior when V2 is active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-gating the removal-cleanup listener in AdminPermissions.java (~77) with Profile.isFeatureEnabled skips cleanup of leftover authorization resources/policies for deleted roles/clients/groups when the feature is disabled, leaving orphaned authz data with no reclamation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the entire ProviderEventListener cleanup logic in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-removal cleanup is wired to a throwing stub: the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which in V2 mode (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled — the PR's target mode and Keycloak's default) lands on ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, so either DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with 500/rollback for every client in FGAP-enabled realms, or if the exception is swallowed the deleted client's authz Resource (named by internal ID), scopes, and attached scope-permissions/policies are permanently orphaned with no working per-client cleanup path anywhere in V2.

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, the `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` branch unconditionally calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). adjudication_records.issue_text: Runtime token-exchange permission check throws instead of evaluating: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, so a grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange request reaching the exchange-permission check in FGAP-enabled realms produces an unhandled 500 instead of an allow/deny decision (security control failing open with a server error rather than denying), previously-configured V1 exchange grants become inoperative, and the new CLIENTS resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema omits the V1 token-exchange scope entirely so the exchange permission can no longer even be created.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ClientPermissionsV2 and wires it into MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(), but several permission-related methods in ClientPermissionsV2 explicitly throw UnsupportedOperationException (e.g., canExchangeTo(), exchangeToPermission(), and others). If any runtime path in V2 calls these (token-exchange is a likely candidate given the existing API), it will crash rather than return an allow/deny decision. Additionally, the new AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS ResourceType scopes omit any token-exchange scope, so there is no schema-supported way (in this diff) to create a token-exchange permission for the new CLIENTS resource type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Other throwing overrides in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, *Permission) will 500 any remaining caller of the legacy per-client permissions API (e.g., the old admin console 'Permissions' tab) in V2 realms.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is newly overridden to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides multiple inherited methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, and several `*Permission(...)` methods). The diff does not show whether such callers (e.g., old admin console permissions UI) still exist/are reachable in V2 realms, so it’s a specific, diff-grounded risk rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Map-roles checks lost the V1 'manage ⇒ map-roles' equivalence with no admin-role fallback: V2 canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles accept only an explicit map-roles/map-roles-composite/map-roles-client-scope FGAP grant, so neither the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role nor a per-client manage/configure grant satisfies them, potentially silently denying routine client-role operations (e.g., composite-role management) to standard realm admins and even full realm admins without explicit FGAP grants in every FGAP-enabled (default) realm — intent and out-of-diff call sites must be verified before merge.

adjudication.rationale: In the new V2 implementation, `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles(...)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(...)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(...)` return only `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` and do not include any fallback for admin roles (e.g., `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS`) nor do they treat `MANAGE`/`CONFIGURE` as sufficient. This is directly visible in `ClientPermissionsV2` where other methods explicitly check admin roles (e.g., `canManage(ClientModel)` and `canManageClientScopes()`), but the map-roles methods do not. If any REST/admin operations rely on these `canMap*` checks (not shown in the diff), users with traditional admin roles could be denied unless explicit FGAP permissions exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:125-145) performs an unbounded findByType scan of every Clients-type resource in the realm's admin resource server, running a full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission) per resource — including potential lazy loads from resource.getScopes() inside the loop — and materializing the entire granted set into a HashSet regardless of the request's pagination; this N+1 pattern costs O(#client-resources × evaluation cost) on every admin client list request, recomputed from scratch each time even though permission grants rarely change

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission (new file), the method iterates all resources of type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE via resourceStore.findByType(...) and for each resource calls hasGrantedPermission(...), which invokes root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server). This is a per-resource policy evaluation inside the scan and the results are accumulated into a HashSet, with no pagination or short-circuiting visible in this method. That is a diff-grounded potential N+1 / O(N * evaluation) performance concern, though the claim that it runs "on every admin client list request" is not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission checks in ClientPermissionsV2 (lines 57-88, 117-122, ~213-221) run redundant, un-memoized full evaluations within a single check: a denied canView(client) triggers up to four independent full evaluations, canView(ClientScopeModel) evaluates the same type resource twice when one evaluation's returned Collection<Permission> already contains every granted scope, and hasPermission(ClientModel, String) issues a policy-store findByResource emptiness probe whose answer the subsequent evaluation would already provide; nothing caches type-resource or per-client evaluation results, multiplying the cost on the hot admin path where getAccess flows call several canXxx methods per client

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ClientPermissionsV2 with multiple permission-check methods that each call hasPermission(...) which performs a full root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...)) evaluation. In particular, canView(ClientModel) calls canView() and canConfigure(client) before falling back to hasPermission(client, VIEW), and canConfigure(client) itself may call canManage(client) then hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE); each of these paths triggers separate evaluatePermission calls with no memoization. Also canView(ClientScopeModel) does hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE), which evaluates the same type resource twice. Additionally, hasPermission(ClientModel,String) does a policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() probe on the “all-clients” resource before running evaluatePermission; this is an extra store query that could be avoided since the subsequent evaluation result already indicates granted scopes (or none). This is a concrete performance/architecture concern visible in the added code, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is incompatible with V2's throwing setPermissionsEnabled: the AdminPermissions.java listener (~78-95) still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on client removal, which throws UnsupportedOperationException in ClientPermissionsV2 (~191-195); if the listener receives the V2 evaluator while FGAP is enabled, every client deletion throws from inside the event listener and rolls back the delete, and if it receives the V1 implementation, V2 type-'Clients' resources and their associated policies for deleted clients are never (or only partially) cleaned up, accumulating orphaned authz rows without bound

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). The diff introduces ClientPermissionsV2, where setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) is overridden to always throw UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2 ~lines 191-195). MgmtPermissionsV2 is also extended to return ClientPermissionsV2 from clients(). If the V2 management implementation is used under the enabled feature, the listener will throw during client removal, which is a clear runtime correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal-event cleanup in AdminPermissions.java:78 is now gated on the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag (previously it ran unconditionally), so a deployment that used FGAP and later disables the feature will leak resource/policy rows for every subsequently removed client, role, or group — inert rows that grow the authz tables without bound and slow findByType scans if the feature is ever re-enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener(...)`, the entire removal-event handler is now wrapped in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously, `RoleRemovedEvent`/`ClientRemovedEvent`/`GroupRemovedEvent` always triggered `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`, which is the only cleanup hook shown in this diff for permissions artifacts when those models are deleted. With the new gating, if FGAP was previously enabled (so permissions resources/policies could exist) and later the feature is disabled, subsequent removals will skip this cleanup path, leaving stale authorization data behind until/unless the feature is re-enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException whenever V2 is active — the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.java (~89-95) still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but with the feature enabled clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws 'Not supported in V2', causing DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} to fail with 500 and a rolled-back transaction (and leaking per-client 'Clients' permission resources if the exception is swallowed); the V2 override should clean up or no-op, never throw from a listener-invoked method.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is overridden to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). If the V2 permissions implementation is used under the enabled feature (as implied by the new MgmtPermissionsV2 override), client deletion will trigger this listener path and can fail with an uncaught exception during the remove event handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: UnsupportedOperationException thrown from runtime permission evaluators instead of failing closed — canExchangeTo (ClientPermissionsV2.java:147) and the rest of the UOE family (~151-204: exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) are runtime evaluator surfaces consulted by V1 cross-client token-exchange and admin REST endpoints (getAccess, per-client management-permission endpoints); throwing converts what should be a deny (403) or feature-gated 4xx into an HTTP 500 whenever V2 is active — permission checks must fail closed (return false) or the call sites must be provably unreachable/gated in V2 mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a new runtime implementation, `ClientPermissionsV2`, and wires it in via `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` to be returned at runtime. In `ClientPermissionsV2`, a large set of overridden methods (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. The diff does not show any feature-gating or call-site changes proving these methods are never invoked when V2 is active, so this creates a concrete risk of runtime 500s if any existing admin REST / permission-management paths still call them. However, the finding’s assertion that these are definitively consulted by specific V1 endpoints/call flows cannot be verified from this diff alone (those call sites are not in the shown changes), so it’s best classified as a diff-grounded architecture/correctness concern rather than a confirmed, reproducible bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Feature-gating the removal listener (AdminPermissions.java ~78) silently disables permission-resource cleanup in the default feature-off mode — previously RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handlers ran unconditionally deleting removed entities' V1 permission resources and dependent policies from the realm-management authorization server; now with the flag off (the default for a preview feature) nothing is cleaned, and with the flag on the roles()/groups() branches run V1 implementations against the V2 resource server (root.realmResourceServer()), so V1 cleanup effectively never happens in either mode, accumulating orphaned resources/policies unboundedly; if V1 permission management is dead the listener body should be removed rather than gated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the provider removal listener in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` to run only when `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is true (wraps the entire RoleRemoved/ClientRemoved/GroupRemoved handling). This unconditionally prevents any cleanup action when the feature is off, whereas previously these events were always handled. Additionally, the PR introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. The listener still calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`, which would break cleanup (and potentially fail the event handling) if `management(...)` resolves to the V2 permissions implementation when the feature is enabled. The finding’s broader claims about “V1 cleanup never happens” and V1-vs-V2 resource server mismatch are not fully verifiable from this diff alone, but the gating + unsupported cleanup path are diff-grounded behavior risks/defects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Enabling the feature flips client-permission semantics with no migration for existing V1 grants — V2 evaluators (ClientPermissionsV2.java:63-121: canManage/canView/canConfigure/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles, via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()) consult only admin roles plus the new 'Clients' schema store and do not consult V1 per-client grants (realm-management manage/configure/view/map-roles scopes), so flipping the preview feature on silently revokes those grants (allow → deny, operations start returning 403) with no migration step, error hint, or release-note documentation visible; needs an explicit migration/doc note or a compatibility evaluation during the V1→V2 transition.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new V2 evaluation path for clients: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2’s per-client checks (canManage/canConfigure/canView/canMapRoles/...) rely on admin roles plus hasPermission(...) against AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients") resources/scopes. In this diff, ClientPermissionsV2 does not delegate to any prior per-client permission evaluation logic (it only calls super for some *global* checks like canManage()/canView()), and its hasPermission lookup is keyed specifically to the new schema resource type/name conventions. No migration/compatibility fallback or documentation mechanism is shown in the diff. This is a concrete transition/backward-compatibility concern created by the change, but the diff alone doesn’t prove a functional defect without knowing how/where V1 grants were stored/evaluated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client deletion with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled routes the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener (AdminPermissions.java ~90-92) into ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (~191-194), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException — since the listener guard and the V2 selection share the same feature flag, every client deletion either propagates the exception and fails/rolls back DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}, or the exception is swallowed and cleanup silently never runs while logging a stack trace

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, a ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent triggers `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` (AdminPermissions.java). The diff also introduces MgmtPermissionsV2 overriding `clients()` to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, and in ClientPermissionsV2 `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (“Not supported in V2”). If the feature-enabled code path selects MgmtPermissionsV2 (as implied by adding the V2 class and override), then client deletion would invoke this throwing method during cleanup, breaking deletion or causing noisy failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No resource lifecycle for per-client permission resources: AdminPermissionsSchema getOrCreateResource/resolveClient create per-client resources but nothing ever deletes a client's resource (or its scope-permission policies) when the client is removed, causing unbounded growth of orphaned authorization store rows, wasted hasGrantedPermission evaluation of stale resources on every filtered client listing in getClientsWithPermission (which can surface deleted clients' UUIDs in the granted set), and findByName lookups hitting dead rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce per-client resource resolution for the new CLIENTS resource type (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient / getOrCreateResource), but the finding’s core claim that “nothing ever deletes” client-related authorization data on client removal is not verifiable from this diff. The diff explicitly handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent in AdminPermissions.registerListener by calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), which is at least a lifecycle hook for cleanup/disable. Whether that call actually deletes resources/policies (or leaves orphans) depends on implementations not shown in the diff, so assertions about unbounded orphaned rows and stale UUIDs being returned cannot be confirmed solely from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V2 UnsupportedOperationException stubs in ClientPermissionsV2 (~150-204: canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRoles*Permission, resource, getPermissions) remain reachable from live request paths outside the new model — token exchange and the legacy client management-permissions REST endpoints now hit unhandled UOE resulting in HTTP 500 instead of the previously inherited functioning V1 implementations, with the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import and dead getEvaluationContext (~260) indicating unfinished stub work
The Clients ResourceType omits a token-exchange scope entirely, so with both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and TOKEN_EXCHANGE enabled, token exchanges can neither be granted nor denied gracefully

However, the new V2 implementation explicitly marks token exchange as unsupported: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canExchangeTo(...) and exchangeToPermission(...) to throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Given this, the omission of a token-exchange scope for CLIENTS is consistent with token exchange not being part of V2 permissions at all, so the finding’s claim about being unable to grant/deny token exchange “gracefully” is not a verifiable defect from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The feature gate in AdminPermissions.java (~78) silently disables stale-resource cleanup when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is off: the role/client/group cleanup listener previously ran unconditionally but is now skipped, so deployments that previously enabled FGAP and later disabled the feature no longer clean up leftover authorization data on role/client/group deletions

adjudication.rationale: The diff in AdminPermissions.registerListener wraps all deletion-event handling (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent) inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }`. Previously these cleanup calls (`setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)`) ran unconditionally. So the finding is accurate that with the feature disabled, this listener no longer performs that cleanup, which could leave stale authorization data if the feature had been enabled before. However, the diff suggests this gating may be intentional (cleanup tied to the feature), and the impact is primarily on data hygiene/re-enablement scenarios rather than an immediate functional break when the feature is off.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String)'s fallback calls getResourceTypeResource, which can create the type resource as a side effect of a read-only permission check (writes-on-read), though it mirrors the existing users V2 pattern and is idempotent

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client `Resource` exists (`resourceStore.findByName(...)` returns null), the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles check only the explicit fine-grained scope with no MANAGE_CLIENTS role check or canManage(client) fallback (unlike V1 which delegated map-roles to manage), silently dropping the 'manage implies map-roles' contract — nothing pins this behavior, and a plain manage-clients admin could get 403 on role mapping under V2; either the implication is intended (needs a test asserting manage ⇒ map-roles) or it's a bug (needs a fix)

adjudication.rationale: In the added `ClientPermissionsV2`, the role-mapping checks are implemented as strict fine-grained-scope checks only: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` each return only `hasPermission(client, ...)` (no `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` and no `canManage(client)` fallback). This is visibly different from how other abilities are handled in V2 (e.g., `canManage(ClientModel)` grants on `MANAGE_CLIENTS`), so it creates an unpinned behavioral decision: whether `MANAGE_CLIENTS` (or `MANAGE`) should implicitly allow role-mapping operations. The diff does not add any test asserting either intended behavior, so reviewers can reasonably request an explicit test or an explicit rationale/adjustment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope is added but never tested anywhere — the test class doesn't import it, no test grants or denies it, and the client scope-mappings role path it guards (canMapClientScopeRoles) is never exercised, so broken wiring for this scope would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (returns `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Thirteen V1 API surface methods (canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, managePermission, viewPermission, resource, getPermissions, exchangeToPermission, mapRoles*Permission) unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException when V2 is active, but no test asserts callers/endpoints handle this gracefully rather than 500-ing, nor that token exchange behaves sanely under V2 config — this entire reachable surface ships unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` where multiple overridden methods unconditionally `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRoles*Permission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). adjudication_records.issue_text: The reworked registerListener removal-cleanup path in AdminPermissions.java is untested — no test exercises deletion of a client that has V2 permission resources/policies attached and asserts they're cleaned up (or that deletion doesn't error), and since V2's setPermissionsEnabled throws, whether the listener dispatches to V1 or V2 on ClientRemovedEvent is safety-critical and unverified

adjudication.rationale: Diff introduces a new V2 client permission evaluator where cleanup-style APIs are explicitly unsupported (ClientPermissionsV2#setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException). However, AdminPermissions.registerListener() still unconditionally dispatches ClientRemovedEvent to management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client,false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests permanently mutate shared state without restoring it (myclient is renamed and has a default client scope removed/re-added as optional, myadmin gets client roles and composite mappings never removed, roles myclient-role/myclient-subRole are never cleaned), creating JUnit method-order dependence where a reorder or new intervening test can produce unrelated failures and the token-scope mutation can silently change authorization behavior in later tests

adjudication_records.issue_text: resolveClient's clientId-string fallback lookup path in AdminPermissionsSchema is untested — no client test creates a permission using the client's clientId string (all use myclient.getId()), so the fallback could be dead or broken (or collide when one client's clientId equals another entity's identifier) without detection

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative/other-user policy enforcement tests for the Clients permission type — every client test grants a policy that matches the caller, and there is no test where the permission's policy targets a different user asserting the caller is still denied, so it's unproven that policies are actually enforced rather than resource existence granting access

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission-evaluation logic copy-pasted three times in ClientPermissionsV2 (lines 221-231, 246-257, 273-283): the 'evaluate ResourcePermission -> nested loop -> match scope' block is duplicated verbatim in hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String), and the isAdminSameRealm()/realmResourceServer() guard preamble appears 4x (including getClientsWithPermission); the copies have already drifted (expectedScopes.contains(s) with a gratuitous single-element Arrays.asList(scope) vs. scope.equals(s)). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ClientPermissionsV2 with duplicated permission-evaluation blocks: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) and hasPermission(String) both call root.evaluatePermission(...) then iterate permissions/scopes using a single-element Arrays.asList(scope) + contains check, while hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String) repeats the same nested loop but uses scope.equals(s) (ClientPermissionsV2 around the shown methods). adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator mixes three concerns — permission evaluation, V1 per-entity permission-resource management, and V1 token-exchange wiring — so ClientPermissionsV2 must stub 12 inherited methods with UnsupportedOperationException (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions), an LSP violation; setPermissionsEnabled — a management mutator — even sits on the evaluator interface (ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:33). Split the interface (evaluation vs. management).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows a new V2 implementation (`ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions`) that must override a large set of inherited methods and implement them as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc. in `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). This is diff-grounded evidence that the base type/API forces V2 to carry V1-specific management/token-exchange responsibilities it does not support. Additionally, the evaluator interface includes mutators like `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` (in `ClientPermissionEvaluator.java`), supporting the claim that evaluation and management concerns are mixed. This is primarily an architectural/LSP/design issue rather than a directly provable functional defect from the diff alone (it becomes a bug only if those unsupported methods are invoked at runtime, which cannot be confirmed solely from this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The ClientRemovedEvent branch in AdminPermissions (~line 92) still calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 stubs to throw, while this PR re-wires MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() (lines 63-69) to return the V2 class and the removal listener is gated by the fine-grained-authz feature flag; if AdminPermissions.management() resolves to the V2 root in feature-enabled deployments, every client deletion throws mid-delete (a P1-level risk). Similar latent exposure exists for canExchangeTo (token-exchange flow) and the V1 permission-management endpoints. Make the listener resilient (no-op or real cleanup in V2) instead of throwing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` now gates the removal listener behind `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` but still executes `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`. In the same PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2#setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is implemented as `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If `management(...)` resolves to the V2 permissions root when the feature is enabled (which is consistent with adding `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()`), client deletion would trigger this listener and throw at runtime during the event handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2 has no resource-cleanup path: orphaned per-client 'Clients' resources accumulate, and even if the removal listener currently routes to V1, cleanup of V2-shaped data depends on the V1 class the V2 stubs disclaim — an undocumented cross-version dependency.
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: fine-grained authz V2 cleanup depends on V1-gated logic, so when V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the removal listener/cleanup path doesn’t run and permission/resources are left orphaned. The candidate frames it as an undocumented cross-version dependency and missing V2 cleanup, which aligns with the golden’s incorrect V1 feature-flag guard causing orphaned permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code copied from V1 into ClientPermissionsV2: unused logger field (line 51), never-called private getEvaluationContext method (lines 260-270), unused static import TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46), unused org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope import (line 27), and ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports (lines 22-23, 29) referenced only by the dead method. adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionEvaluator's public interface docs (lines 35-176) are made implementation-conditional: every new javadoc carries 'For V2 only: ...' clauses and {@link}s to AdminPermissionsSchema, ClientPermissionManagement (CONFIGURE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_*), and AdminPermissionManagement (MANAGE_SCOPE/VIEW_SCOPE) internals, so the public abstraction documents two divergent contracts wired to both implementations' constants; interface callers shouldn't need to know which version they hold, and when V1 is removed ~20 doc blocks must be rewritten and the links break (possibly already dangling). adjudication_records.issue_text: Persisted scope identifiers defined in two places: AdminPermissionsSchema (~lines 64-66) defines CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE while V1's ClientPermissionManagement defines CONFIGURE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE_SCOPE; these strings are persisted as scope names in the DB, so both definitions must stay byte-identical forever with nothing enforcing it. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new persisted-looking scope name constants in `AdminPermissionsSchema` (`CONFIGURE`, `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`) and introduces V2 code that evaluates permissions by comparing returned `Permission.getScopes()` strings against those constants (`ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Two inconsistent code paths for the same 'all-clients' type resource in ClientPermissionsV2: the global path (line 241) uses resourceStore.findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) and denies if absent, while the per-client fallback (lines 214-218) uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) plus a policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() pre-check that exists only there; if getResourceTypeResource is get-or-create, a read-only permission check performs a write, and if it can return null, the subsequent findByResource(server, null) NPEs. The implicit invariant (type-level permissions are resource-linked so findByResource sees them) is undocumented and holds in only one path, so future edits to one path will silently diverge from the other.
matched_golden_ids: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) may return null and that the subsequent call to findByResource(server, null) would cause a NullPointerException, which is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment (need defensive null checks before findByResource).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PermissionClientTest tests mutate shared managed state without restoring it: testManageOnlyOneClient (~lines 155-175) permanently renames the shared managed client 'myclient' and removes one of its default client scopes (re-added only as optional), and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient (~lines 298-366) creates client roles with no cleanup while onAfter (lines 75-79) only deletes scope permissions; JUnit method order is non-deterministic within the class, so index-based picks (getDefaultClientScopes().get(0/1)) and any future count assertions become order-dependent. adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest`, `testManageOnlyOneClient` mutates shared realm state by updating the existing client `myclient` (sets a new name and calls `clientResource.update(myclient)`) and by removing a default client scope (`removeDefaultClientScope(defaultClientScopes.get(1).getId())`) without restoring it; it only re-adds that scope as optional (`addOptionalClientScope`) and does not revert the name. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates new client roles (`myclient-role`, `myclient-subRole`) via `realm.admin().clients().get(myclient.getId()).roles().create(...)` with no cleanup. The class `@AfterEach onAfter()` only removes scope permissions from the admin-permissions client and does not undo these realm/client mutations, so subsequent tests in the same class (and potentially other tests sharing the realm) can become order-dependent/flaky, especially with index-based `getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent test-helper API after static-ization in AbstractPermissionTest (lines 54-76, ~116-178): helpers were converted to static and take ManagedClient/ManagedRealm parameters duplicating the base class's own injected client/realm fields (~30 call sites now spell createUserPolicy(realm, client, ...)), yet getPolicies() still uses the instance field, and the new createPermission(ManagedClient, String, String, Set, ...) overloads are instance methods touching no instance state while sibling createAllPermission is static; the mixed static/instance API plus redundant parameter passing invites passing a different ManagedClient than the injected one. adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException when admin-fine-grained-authz is enabled: the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws unconditionally, so every client deletion (admin console, REST, realm import) fails with a 500/rollback — a breakage introduced by this PR since V1 no-op'd gracefully. adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now executes its event-handling logic only when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, and on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. Also in this diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` method throws `UnsupportedOperationException` unconditionally. If the enabled feature path uses `MgmtPermissionsV2` (as the diff suggests by adding the V2 clients() override), deleting a client would trigger the listener and can crash with `UnsupportedOperationException` (500/rollback).

adjudication_records.issue_text: V2 has no cleanup path at all for per-client Clients resources/policies on client deletion: getOrCreateResource lazily creates them, but all the resource-management methods throw, so orphaned resources/policies accumulate and keep being evaluated in getClientsWithPermission() forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds V2 client permissions but leaves cleanup on client deletion broken. `AdminPermissions.registerListener()` now runs only when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, and on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. In V2, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, so the deletion listener would fail at runtime and cannot disable/cleanup any per-client authorization artifacts. Additionally, `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission()` iterates all stored resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and evaluates them, so any orphaned client resources/policies would continue to be considered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token exchange-to flows return a 500 instead of an allow/deny decision when the feature is enabled: canExchangeTo in ClientPermissionsV2 is a runtime enforcement point invoked by TokenExchangeManager on the exchange-to path, but the V2 override throws unconditionally.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides `canExchangeTo(...)` (and related token-exchange permission methods) to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` unconditionally. If any runtime path calls these methods while V2 is active, it would surface as a 500 rather than a deny/allow decision. However, the diff does not show the call site (e.g., `TokenExchangeManager`) or prove that token exchange flows will invoke `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo` when the feature is enabled, so the specific behavioral claim cannot be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The throwing method family in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRoles*Permission) must be confirmed unreachable from still-exposed REST endpoints such as the legacy /clients/{id}/managementPermissions — those call sites are in the truncated part of the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2` as a concrete implementation returned by `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()`, but many inherited/expected operations are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `managePermission`, `viewPermission`, `configurePermission`, `mapRoles*Permission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). The diff does not show the REST endpoint call sites (e.g., `/clients/{id}/managementPermissions`) that might still invoke these methods, so reachability cannot be verified here. This is nonetheless a specific, diff-grounded risk introduced by the change: if any still-exposed endpoint or listener path calls these methods under V2, it would fail at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code in ClientPermissionsV2 indicating an unfinished port: an unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import and an orphaned private getEvaluationContext method that existed solely to build the client-identity evaluation context for exchange.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, there is a static import `import static org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE;` that is never referenced anywhere in the file. Additionally, the private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` is defined but not called from any code path in `ClientPermissionsV2` (all token-exchange related methods currently throw `UnsupportedOperationException`).
