adjudication_records.issue_text: MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role shortcut silently dropped from canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles: V1 short-circuited on hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), but the V2 methods return only hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES*), so a plain manage-clients admin (and even realm-admin) gets 403 assigning client roles, adding role composites, or mapping client-scope roles — a silent privilege regression on feature-enable with no test coverage, and the new interface javadoc misdescribes V1 behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In the new V2 implementation, ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles to return only hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES*), with no admin-role short-circuit (unlike canManage(ClientModel) and canManageClientScopes(), which explicitly allow AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS). From the diff alone, that means a caller who has MANAGE_CLIENTS (or other built-in admin roles) but no fine-grained permission grants would be denied these mapping operations under V2, which is inconsistent with the other V2 permission checks and plausibly a privilege regression when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. The added tests only cover permission-based grants, not the MANAGE_CLIENTS-role path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-gating the removal-event listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener behind Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) stops legacy V1 resource cleanup when the feature is disabled (the default): realms using legacy per-object permissions will permanently orphan authz resources/policies/scopes in the admin resource server whenever a role/client/group with permissions enabled is deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes AdminPermissions.registerListener so that RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent handling (which calls setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) only runs when Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is true. Previously these cleanup/disable calls ran unconditionally. With this change, when the feature flag is off, deletions will no longer trigger setPermissionsEnabled(false) for roles/clients/groups, which can plausibly leave any previously-created admin-authz artifacts for those objects uncleaned/orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission() pollutes the granted-id set: resourceStore.findByType(server, 'Clients') also visits the type resource itself, so when an all-clients permission grants the scope the literal string 'Clients' is added to a set documented as containing client ids.
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: getClientsWithPermission() uses resourceStore.findByType(..., 'Clients') and adds resource.getName() into a set intended to contain client IDs. This ends up including the type-level 'Clients' resource name rather than actual client IDs, which then breaks downstream code expecting real client IDs (e.g., realm.getClientById).

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission() never enumerates clients authorized only via the all-clients type resource — it returns nothing useful exactly when the admin holds a realm-wide grant, so consumers relying on this set alone render silently empty lists (only the per-client MANAGE-scope path is covered by testManageOnlyOneClient).

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission(), the method only iterates existing authorization Resources of type "Clients" and adds resource.getName() to the result. For realm-wide grants created via the resource-type ("all-clients") resource, the only matching resource may be the type-level resource whose name is AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE (i.e., "Clients"), not individual client IDs. The method does not expand a realm-wide grant into the set of actual client IDs, so callers expecting a set of client identifiers will not get the clients authorized solely via the all-clients resource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-create race in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource: there is no uniqueness enforcement on resource names, so two concurrent permission creations referencing the same client (or concurrent lazy creation of the 'Clients' type resource on deny paths) can create duplicate same-named resources; subsequent findByName lookups return an arbitrary duplicate, making grants attached to one copy intermittently invisible to hasPermission (fail-closed, hard-to-reproduce 403s). This PR widens the race's blast radius to every per-client permission check and makes deny paths perform store writes as a side effect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show (or modify) the internal implementation of AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource in a way that demonstrates a check-then-create race or lack of uniqueness enforcement on resource names. The PR mainly adds a new CLIENTS resource type, new scopes, client ID resolution, and new permission-evaluation logic in ClientPermissionsV2 that performs reads (resourceStore.findByName, policyStore.findByResource, evaluatePermission). While the finding asserts that deny paths now perform store writes as a side effect, the only potentially-creating call mentioned (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource) is not shown here, so the claimed write side effect and duplicate-resource behavior cannot be verified from the diff alone.
